questions.topic: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space
questions.question: What does Rocchio relevance feedback update?
options: The query vector, using the centroids of the judged documents
The document vectors, using the centroid of the original query
The collection token counts, using the clicks a result received
The index vocabulary, using the terms found in the feedback set

questions.topic: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space
questions.question: What role does alpha play in the Rocchio formula?
options: It weights only the centroid of the judged nonrelevant documents
It preserves the influence of the user's original query wording
It fixes the number of expansion terms the update may keep
It sets the similarity cutoff used to select the top results

questions.topic: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space
questions.question: Relevant vectors are [1,1] and [0,2]. What is their centroid?

questions.topic: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space
questions.question: Why is gamma often smaller than beta in practice?
options: Relevant documents rarely contain any terms worth adding
Gamma must be set to exactly zero by the Rocchio formula
Negative feedback lengthens the query beyond the index limit
Nonrelevant documents can fail for many unrelated reasons

questions.topic: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space
questions.question: For q=[1,0], relevant centroid=[0.5,1.5], nonrelevant centroid=[0,1], alpha=1, beta=0.8, gamma=0.2, what is the update?

questions.topic: Rocchio Relevance Feedback in Vector Space
questions.question: Why can Rocchio drift on a query with two distinct valid intents?
options: It cannot represent weighted vectors, only binary term presence
A single centroid can land midway between the two separate clusters
It discards the original query vector at every feedback round
The update keeps only the highest-weight terms, dropping the rest

questions.question: What assumption defines pseudo-relevance feedback?
options: Every document in the collection is treated as relevant evidence
Users explicitly label every result before the second pass runs
The top initial results are treated as relevant without judgments
Only the documents judged nonrelevant are allowed to supply terms

questions.question: What does RM3 combine?
options: Two unrelated document rankings taken from separate indexes
The nonrelevant document vectors and the collection statistics
A per-document latency score and its recorded click count
The original query model and a relevance model from feedback

questions.question: What is the main failure mode of pseudo-relevance feedback?
options: It amplifies errors in the initial ranking into query drift
It adds no new vocabulary beyond the terms already typed
It requires every collection document to be judged first
It returns a second-pass ranking identical to the first

questions.question: Why should feedback depth and expansion-term count be tuned jointly?
options: Neither choice changes the cost of the second retrieval pass
Both trade evidence coverage against noise and added latency
Both are fixed by the identifiers stored in the index segments
Raising either one always improves the final ranking metric

questions.question: Original query weight is 0.6, original P(database)=0.5, and feedback P(database)=0.2. What is the interpolated probability?
What does the gap between oracle feedback and pseudo-feedback performance diagnose?
options: The character count produced by the document tokenizer
The number of terms the original query happened to contain
Whether the evaluation metric is binary or graded relevance
The cost of selecting the feedback documents imperfectly

questions.topic: Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
questions.question: What common objective connects classic feedback and modern query expansion?
options: Bridging the vocabulary gap between the need and the documents
Lengthening every query regardless of what the user intended
Removing the original query evidence before the second pass
Replacing relevance evaluation with generated answer passages

questions.topic: Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
questions.question: What distinguishes local from global expansion?
options: Local expansion never consults any documents, only a thesaurus file
Local uses this query's results; global uses collection resources
Global expansion needs user judgments collected for each query
Global expansion is unable to introduce synonyms of any kind

questions.topic: Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
questions.question: Why retain an original-query retrieval channel alongside generated expansion?
options: Generated text always keeps exact identifiers intact and unaltered
The original query carries no lexical value once expansion runs
It protects exact evidence and limits drift toward another intent
It stops the two candidate lists from being fused by their scores

questions.topic: Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
questions.question: Why can five similar rewrites provide less value than intent-diverse rewrites?
options: Similar rewrites are always shorter than diverse ones would be
Only one rewrite can be sent to the inverted index at a time
Diversity removes every false positive from the candidate set
Repeated paraphrases amplify one mistaken reading of the query

questions.topic: Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
questions.question: Expansion improves broad questions but harms exact product codes. What is the best operational response?
options: Route expansion by query class and keep exact-match candidates
Disable exact lexical retrieval across the whole search stack
Evaluate only the broad questions and report that average
Generate even more expansion terms for every product code

questions.topic: Relevance Feedback as the Ancestor of Modern Query Expansion
questions.question: Why must access control be applied before extracting expansion evidence?
options: Expansion terms are always drawn from the query, never from documents
Inaccessible documents could leak vocabulary into permitted results
Access control is applied again when the final results are rendered
Feedback extraction can only ever run over fully public documents
